profile.headline: Full-stack Developer happily employed at Columbia Insurance Group
profile.summary:
For over a decade, I have been designing lighting for events and corporate meetings. Having first studied and trained at the University of North Carolina School of the Arts which gave me the not only a design background but the skills necessary to work plan and execute large scale projects under intense pressure. This allowed me to succeed also as a production and project manager where I coordinated the different aspects that make up a production including audio, video, scenery, decor, catering and the many other parts needed to create a successful event.

I love the creative process and figuring out how to put the puzzle pieces together,  the process of partnering with my clients and various teams to ultimately give the guests an experience to remember.

Now, as I work my way through the WeCanCodeIT coding bootcamp, I’m learning new skills that still relate to the work I’ve done for so many years. Coding is my new puzzle and I still have the opportunity to work in a creative team environment as we look for solutions for our clients. I am able to apply my detail oriented and analytical skills to find creative solutions to complex problems. I am able to manage multiple projects in a deadline-driven environment without breaking a sweat and work with other people to troubleshoot and debug issues.

When I’m not solving challenges at work, I’m enjoying time with my two kids and wife. When time permits, I enjoy photography, house projects and I’m currently building a kit car.

Specialties: Lighting Design, Organizing, Negotiating, AutoCad 2010, Vectorworks, Unique Business Systems R2,  Adobe Lightroom, basic Adobe Photoshop Skills, Quickbooks, Java, Spring, Hibernate, TDD, JavaScript, jQuery, HTML5, CSS3, Flexbox, MVC, Responsive/Mobile-First Design, Structured Query Language (SQL), Transactional Databases/ MSSQL, Object Oriented Programming, Git, MS Access

projects.title: R2 Implementation  @ Bartha
projects.description:
Unique Business Systems R2 Rental Inventory Software Implementation.
Goal: Solid implementation within a year without any challenges I experienced with previous implementations of R2.
Status: Success!

I began with reviewing existing data. I created a Microsoft Access Database, using my existing experience building Access Databases and teaching myself basic VBA to enhance the database. While one would think putting it into Excel would be easier, I believed organizing the data in Access allowed easier normalization and review of the data for multiple users across the company. Best of all, using the software import specifications I was able to set limits to the data allowing us to validate the data before import. Once all of the data was reviewed and normalized, I simply ran my exports to create files needed by Unique Business Systems. Their review time was cut down and the import process went fairly smoothly.

When it came to create custom forms, I was able to save Bartha significant money by creating the forms in-house. I already had a basic understanding of how the forms were created from my past experience at The Show Factory, Inc. Once I had the reference documentation needed, I was able to create the code needed to generate custom forms that we could easily adjust. Again, I turned to Microsoft Access to create a small database application that would help me generate the lines of code to format the initial forms.

It took about a year of careful planning and many meetings, but it paid off with a fairly simple transition without any regression or major difficulties. We are currently fully operational and already beginning to take advantage of more advanced functionalities of the software. This has allowed me to reduce my role to managing and fine tuning the software and expand my role at the company as a Full Stack Developer where I will work on building in-house applications that can integrate with R2 and also independent applications.

projects.title: Buckeye Miata Club Time Keeper Database v0
projects.description:
For years, Buckeye Miata Club used a Microsoft Excel spreadsheet to enter driver lap times for their AutoCross events. It served its purpose but it was slow to get drivers registered and made tabulating data at the end of the season a challenge.

Goal: To speed up registration process; get cars on the grid faster; track lap times easily; race results could be calculated at the push of a button and the race season can be easily calculated.
Status: Success with some refinements on-going.

In a club meeting it came up that we wanted a better solution for keeping track of timing without spending a lot of money on an application that we may or may not like. I have a strange love of creating access databases and volunteered to create a new application for the 2017 race season.

I broke the project down into segments, starting with driver registration and then adding tables as I went. I went more in depth with VBA programming than I had ever done since I had a better understanding of functions and basic programming after having started an online introductory computer science course (CS50x).

I was able to get what I considered a beta version ready for our first event, a casual fun event, and I was pretty happy with the results. The first time around, it took awhile to register drivers but the benefit was that for the first official event, registration didn’t take that long because drivers were already in the system. Each event I was able to address bugs and add enhancements and features. By the end of the season, we were able to quickly print up race results and calculate season standing.

We are still considering the app as in beta as we continue to test live but the plan is for me to create a new app from the ground up once I complete my Full Stack Development training completed. We want to be able to provide a solution where drivers can easily look up their times and race results.
